Bedlam

BED-luhm -- from 'Bethlehem,' the name of a former London hospital for the mentally ill. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Bedlam is a scene of wild uproar and confusion.

The backstage hallway was pure bedlam ten minutes before the show, with costumes, cues, and last-minute rewrites flying everywhere.

Worked Example

The instant the power went out during the championship game, every phone flashlight came on, people started shouting directions in the dark, and someone knocked over an entire table of concession snacks.

That sudden, noisy, out-of-control chaos -- with everyone shouting and nothing under control -- is exactly what bedlam describes.

How Bedlam Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

chaos

chaos: complete disorder and confusion

pandemonium

pandemonium: wild uproar, as if a whole crowd had lost control

Antonyms

tranquility

tranquility: a state of calm and peacefulness

orderliness

orderliness: a well-organized, systematic state

How Strong Is It? — chaos → pandemonium → bedlam

chaos vs. bedlam

chaos vs. bedlam: Chaos simply means a lack of order -- it doesn't necessarily involve noise or people at all, like a chaotic desk covered in papers. Bedlam adds the specific picture of a crowd of people, shouting and moving in every direction.

pandemonium vs. bedlam

pandemonium vs. bedlam: Pandemonium is almost interchangeable with bedlam, though it leans slightly more dramatic and is often used for a single sudden, startling moment, like pandemonium breaking out after a surprise announcement.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — Bedlam

root — Bedlam: a folk-corruption of 'Bethlehem,' after London's St. Mary of Bethlehem psychiatric hospital (Middle English)

Put it together

Put it together: Bedlam began as a nickname for London's Bethlehem hospital, notorious for the noise and disorder inside it -- over time the word drifted from that one building to describe any scene of wild uproar and confusion.

Use the root in a new word: pandemonium

Use the root in a new word: pandemonium: The stadium dissolved into pandemonium after the referee's controversial call reversed the final score.
